Background reading on **prerequisite skills** (R, Unix, single-cell biology, statistics) and the **reference material** the workshop's chapters cite into — computing fundamentals, shell scripting, Git, HPC/Talapas, databases, file formats, and a methods-section template. Read what you need, when you need it.

These materials support the core workshop but are not part of the three-day sequence — they live here in **Additional Resources** so you can reach for them before, during, or long after the workshop.

## Appendices — prerequisite tools and reference

| # | Appendix | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| A | [R Programming Fundamentals](Appendix_A_R_Programming.html) | R basics — data structures, functions, the tidyverse, the package ecosystem |
| B | [Unix & the Command Line](Appendix_B_Unix_Command_Line.html) | Filesystem navigation, common commands, pipes and redirection |

| E | [Computer Systems & Computing Fundamentals](Appendix_E_Computing_Fundamentals.html) | How computers, operating systems, and HPC clusters work |
| F | [GREP, Regular Expressions & Shell Scripting](Appendix_F_GREP_Regex_Shell.html) | Pattern matching with `grep`, regex syntax, writing reusable shell scripts |

| K | [Methods-Section Template](Appendix_K_Methods_Template.html) | Annotated boilerplate for an scRNA-seq paper's methods section |

## How to use these resources

::: callout-tip
**Read the appendices on demand.** The workshop [chapters](../Materials.html) cross-reference the appendices liberally — when a chapter says "see Appendix D § 8 for why per-cell DE fails", that's a hint to read that section before continuing.

**Suggested initial reading order if you're new to the toolchain:** A (R) → B (Unix) → F (GREP & shell) → G (Git) → E (computing fundamentals) → H (Talapas/HPC). Read the *Glossary* alongside the lectures.

**If your molecular biology is rusty:** Appendix C, before Lecture 00.

**If your statistics is rusty:** Appendix D, before Lecture 05 / Chapter 5.

**Once you start writing up your own scRNA-seq results:** keep Appendix K (Methods-Section Template) open in another tab.
:::
